convoLines.text: "I asked Marta about the pantry run — Marta's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the ridge above the creek and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Since Marta died... I keep expecting to see Marta at the fire. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Kelsey. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane… That's Nevermore telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Yarrow. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Marta owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Halfway to the cache spot, Fabiana freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Nobody says Marta's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Purslane — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now, anyway."
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"This one — Desert Date. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"I dreamed Marta was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"I keep turning over the last thing Marta said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Purslane today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Fabiana. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "There. You wanted honest."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"I've changed my mind about people before. Usually it takes getting hurt first. You haven't hurt me yet."
"Still on each other."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Don't laugh. Being the reason someone dies."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You've been singing in the creek. Badly, by your own admission. Heard anything worth stealing yet?"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Kelsey doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind? Gotta keep moving."
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Fabiana: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took you — Riddle Me This, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening. Don't make me repeat it."

"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."

"All right. Thank you for telling me."
